tasks.short: Balance warehouse access, loading and resources

steps.what: Clarify customer requirements, workload characteristics and data warehouse resource constraints
Design the comprehensive warehouse approach balancing access, batch loading and resource utilization

tasks.design: For the design branch of this task, keep requirements and architecture choices with the specialist. Native workload evidence in {DATA_PLATFORM} and decisions in {DOCS} support the trade-off; no automatic optimal warehouse or implementation saving is established.
tasks.previous_blocker: Access and loading objectives can conflict under real resource constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: Monitoring supports evidence gathering but does not choose the appropriate architecture.
tasks.still_hard: Workload representativeness and customer priorities determine which compromise is acceptable.
tasks.human_edge: Expose conflicting goals and propose a design whose limitations are understood.
tasks.altitude: Retain architecture judgement rather than claiming an entire warehouse can be generated from a requirement label.

reach.learn: How workload objectives constrain storage and loading design

evidence.claim: Comprehensive warehouse design depends on customer priorities and representative workload evidence; no measured local automation saving is established.

assumptions: Boundary is the stated design branch, excluding separate implementation and recurring operation. Those alternatives receive no savings attribution from this design.

Customers supply priorities during s1 and existing operations supply workload evidence before or during s1. The specialist checks periods, units, resource constraints and uncertainty within retained time. No free representative-workload, available-capacity or approved-design flag is assumed; missing evidence requires manual investigation before a qualified proposal.
Use native workload views and existing documentation first. No new collection pipeline or work transfer is proposed, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Actual workload evidence and customer trade-off priorities
research_questions: Which design choice changes when loading and access objectives conflict?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0 for the design branch. No implementation or recurring operation baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Program warehouse analysis and system changes

steps.what: Analyze the system requirement and specify program behavior, inputs and expected results
Draft programming code and proposed tests for the specified warehouse change

loop.purpose: Draft implementation in an isolated branch for a specified programming change
loop.input: Versioned requirement, source context and independent expected cases
loop.output: Source diff, proposed tests and explicit assumptions
loop.check: Specialist inspects language semantics, data leakage, error handling and edge cases; independent expected results determine correctness rather than model-generated assertions alone.
loop.stop: One draft and correction pass; unresolved failures return to manual programming. No production access is available.
loop.why_not_simpler: Native transformations and templates cover standard mappings, while a novel specified change may need language-specific code.

steps.what: Test program behavior independently and accept the exact source version for further delivery

tasks.design: For the programming branch, use native {DATA_PLATFORM} transformations first and bounded coding assistance for remaining explicit changes. The specialist establishes expected behavior, reviews the diff and performs independent tests before accepting a development version.
tasks.previous_blocker: First-pass code repeats implementation work after the change is specified.
tasks.enabler_now: Coding assistance supports draft implementation under oversight.
tasks.still_hard: Missing data, semantic errors and incomplete tests can make plausible code incorrect.
tasks.human_edge: Define independent expectations and recognize a test that merely repeats the implementation.
tasks.altitude: Retain analysis and acceptance while reducing first-pass programming effort.

reach.task: Check program behavior against model semantics
reach.learn: How keys, grain and null handling affect correctness

evidence.claim: GitHub Copilot supplies coding and review assistance with oversight expected; this supports drafting rather than autonomous production changes.
Programming studies in the digest show differing productivity results, so the local time estimate remains unmeasured E1.

assumptions: Boundary is programming with necessary analysis and testing, excluding independent exploratory data-analysis engagements and production deployment. The proposed saving applies only to that branch.

Application owners supply requirements and existing developers provide source/schema versions before s1. In s1 the specialist captures language/runtime, source versions, permitted data/actions, input contracts, expected outputs, edge cases and error behavior. Its 30 hours include inspection and expected-case construction; no free complete specification, clean dataset or passed-test flag is assumed. Missing contracts require manual analysis.
Native transformations, reusable functions and existing tests precede model drafting. No additional requirements-entry task is transferred to source owners.
unknowns: Real programming share and approved source access
research_questions: Does draft code save time after source specification, independent tests and rework?

already_counted.description: Independent tests and exact development-version acceptance

approvals.approved_version: Exact source commit, dependency versions and independent test evidence accepted; changes void approval. Production deployment remains separate.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 programming branch B=100, R=82, gross=18, focal upkeep=7, net=11. Range 0-4 allows native transformations, incomplete requirements and expensive generated-code corrections.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Create warehouse metadata and process documentation

steps.what: Verify metadata sources and capture entity relationships, business processes and flow definitions
Create metadata dictionaries and diagrams from the explicit documentation specification
Check documentation against source versions and clarify semantic or process gaps

tasks.design: Generate diagrams and dictionaries through native {DATA_PLATFORM} exports from an explicit specification. {DOCS} holds owner explanations and semantic checks; undocumented business processes are captured by the specialist before rendering.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual diagrams drift from versioned structures and repeated process descriptions.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic rendering can represent specified objects and edges without inferring business meaning.
tasks.still_hard: A technical lineage edge may not represent a real business responsibility or exception path.
tasks.human_edge: Identify what the diagram leaves out and whether its meanings match practice.
tasks.altitude: Maintain source-linked documentation definitions rather than redraw them.

reach.task: Review documentation version and meaning control
reach.learn: How to preserve traceability when source structures change

evidence.claim: Explicit metadata and process graph specifications support deterministic rendering; no local saving or automatic business-process discovery is established.

assumptions: Boundary is supporting documentation, excluding original model design and ongoing metadata-framework operation. Identical export work shared with those tasks is counted once.

Developers supply existing schema/pipeline versions and process owners supply descriptions before or during s1. The specialist captures object/field IDs, types, explicit keys and edges, process steps/owners, conditions, source versions and notation in s1; its 35 hours include manual interviews, reconciliation and capture. No free complete lineage or structured business-process graph is assumed. Unknown edges remain gaps and unsupported constructs are documented manually.
Native metadata exports and diagram templates precede custom code. No new structured-entry task is transferred to process owners.
unknowns: Completeness of process evidence and export compatibility
research_questions: How much rendering effort remains after semantic source capture and diagram checks?

incremental.description: Notation/export maintenance and unsupported construct handling

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B=100, R=60, gross=40, focal upkeep=8, net=32. Range 0-15 allows existing generation and extensive manual capture of business semantics.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Create metadata framework definitions, ownership, change rules and exception handling with relevant owners
Implement and check the specified metadata process using native catalog configuration

tasks.design: Create the framework with its owners and configure native catalog facilities in {DATA_PLATFORM}; preserve definitions and exceptions in {DOCS}. This design retains implementation effort and claims no future metadata operation saving as current framework-development time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Metadata responsibilities and update rules require explicit agreement before configuration.
tasks.enabler_now: Native catalog forms and workflow facilities can implement known rules without a new autonomous model.
tasks.still_hard: Ownership disputes, exceptions and semantic changes require decisions beyond field validation.
tasks.human_edge: Determine who is accountable for a definition and how disagreement is resolved.
tasks.altitude: Design a maintainable ownership process without assuming that its inputs already exist.

reach.task: Define ownership and version control for metadata
reach.learn: How change procedures preserve meaning and accountability

evidence.claim: Native catalog configuration can represent explicit metadata processes; the new process does not establish a current-task labour reduction.

assumptions: Boundary is framework creation and implementation, excluding recurring metadata operation and original business data capture. Existing configuration is the baseline means; no new add-on or rollout beyond this task is proposed.

Owners supply needs and responsibility constraints during s1; the specialist captures definitions, required fields, owners, validation rules, versioning and exceptions within its 60 hours. S2 retains configuration, testing and owner clarification. No free approved taxonomy, complete ownership register or valid-metadata flag is assumed; unresolved governance prevents activation of the affected rule.

Native catalog facilities precede custom code. Initial configuration and tests remain in s2; no changed recurring process or transferred capture duty is assumed, so incremental upkeep for this unchanged approach is zero.
unknowns: Native catalog capability and actual authority over metadata processes
research_questions: Which metadata exceptions require owner decisions rather than a validation rule?

already_counted.description: Native implementation, tests and exact configuration acceptance

incremental.description: No added process beyond retained framework implementation

approvals.approved_version: Exact metadata schema, ownership assignments, access, validation, versioning and exception configuration accepted within delegated authority; changes require renewed specialist review and existing owner approval where required.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Framework design and implementation retain their time; future operation savings are outside this task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Generate specified code and documentation while retaining warehouse trade-offs, independent validation and metadata governance.
reach: Discuss architecture choices with database architects
Clarify metadata accountability with document management specialists
skills_to_grow: Record metadata ownership and exception decisions
role.ambitious_version: A warehouse specialist whose representations are reproducible and whose architectural and governance choices remain explicit.
